items.q: What is the WAT framework in Claude Code?
items.a: **Workflows** are natural-language markdown recipes; **Tools** are Python scripts (ingredients); the **Agent** (Claude Code) reads workflows and invokes tools in order. Both improve as the agent learns from mistakes.

items.q: Why start ambiguous builds in plan mode?
items.a: **Plan mode** makes Claude ask clarifying questions before building. Read and **edit the plan** before auto-accepting — don't let the agent run blind on fuzzy requests.

items.q: Where should API keys live during builds?
items.a: Never paste secrets into chat. Put Perplexity, Gmail, and similar keys in **`.env` placeholders** the agent creates for you.

items.q: Why do live sessions feel smarter than deployed automations?
items.a: Live agents can **self-heal mid-run**. Deployed systems (GitHub → trigger.dev/modal/Vercel) ship **workflows + tools only**, not the live agent — so **battle-test before shipping**.

items.q: What are the five Claude Code surfaces?
items.a: **Terminal** (most power), **desktop app** (GUI + scheduled tasks), **web** at claude.ai/code (runs when laptop is off), and **IDE extensions** (VS Code/Cursor/Antigravity) — all wrapping the same engine.

items.q: What are Claude Code skills actually?
items.a: **Skills = loadable SOPs** (front-end design, custom infographics, etc.). The agent decides when to invoke based on **description matching** the task.

items.q: When do sub-agents and agent teams help?
items.a: **Sub-agents** handle specialized subtasks; **agent teams** coordinate parallel work (CLI-only features like `/agents`).

items.q: Why prefer saved API docs over MCP sometimes?
items.a: **API reference docs often beat MCP** — research once, save endpoints locally, and burn fewer tokens than loading full MCP schemas every session.

items.q: How should you position Claude Code work to clients?
items.a: Act as the **doctor, not the pharmacist** — sell diagnosis and ROI (**save 20 hrs/week**), not "I build Claude Code workflows." Avoid hourly once value is proven.

items.q: What does value-based pricing look like in practice?
items.a: If a system saves a client **$10K/month**, charge about **$5K** for the build — roughly **two-week payback** for them and strong margin for you. A **30-minute build** that saves **20 hours/week** is not a 30-minute job.

items.q: Why still learn n8n/Zapier if agents are the future?
items.a: Agentic workflows may grow from **$7B → ~$93B**, but **n8n/Zapier fundamentals** still matter — you need plumbing literacy to spot bad agent decisions. People who skip fundamentals and jump straight to Claude Code struggle.
